data.reason: Review round 1 passed with two low findings that Ruud chose to fix before delivery: F1, a docstring paragraph of finding_identities still states SEEN-145's line-then-id tie order as if it decided a join; F2, the property test never draws two findings sharing an id, so the same-id field is not tested for order independence

findings.claim: One paragraph of the finding_identities docstring was left as SEEN-145 wrote it. It says the finding at the same line, and then the one under the same id, takes a later finding that matches two equally well. Since this change, the number of joins and the number of shared texts are both weighed before line or id.
findings.failure_scenario: Take a later finding that matches identity A at the same line and identity B at another line, sharing one text with each. If giving it to B lets another finding of the same record join A, the search gives it to B. The paragraph at lines 300 to 303 says A takes it, so a reader of that paragraph alone expects the wrong join, although the paragraph at lines 305 to 325 states the true order.

findings.claim: The property test names findings F<index> in record 1 and G<index> in record 2. No drawn pair ever shares an id, so the same-id part of the strength and of the tie-break is never exercised for order independence.
findings.failure_scenario: Suppose a later change made the same-id field depend on position. For example, a tie between two same-id candidates broken by list index. Records drawn with shared ids would then count differently by order, but this test draws none and would stay green.
